chapter_theme: A yogic song at Thirunallur (திருநல்லூர்): the poet describes the ascent from the root centre through the three mandalas and bindu and nada, up the central pillar on the rope of knowledge, and asks whether he will meet the light of a hundred crore moons; the praise names the goddess and the saint who imposed the ash on the Jains.

762.reading: The poet describes an inner ascent: the root centre and the mantra of experience, the supreme lights of the three mandalas, the six centres, the boundless light of a thousand rays, bindu and nada, the sound of 'Olam' kept to many rhythms, the nectar drunk, the course of moon, sun and fire stilled, and the climb up the middle pillar on the rope of knowledge, and asks whether he will not meet the light of a hundred crore moons. The praise names the goddess by many names, Murugan as destroyer of Sura and helper of Indra, who dances to the sound of the Veda, the lotus-handed one who put sacred ash on so that the Jains who refused it died on the stake, the lover of Devayanai and the doe, at Nallur where Siva as Thiyagar dwells.
762.nuance: The plea is a single question (சத கோடி சந்த்ர ஒளி சந்தியாதோ) at the top of a ladder of yogic terms: மூலம், மண்டலம் மூணு, விந்து நாதம், நடு தூண் (the central channel), ஞான வண் கயிறு. சீல வெண்பொடி இடாத வெஞ்சமணர் மாள ... நீறிடும் is the Sambandar story again. Many compounds in the first half split uncertainly.

links.note: Both picture the yogi running up the central staff to the head through the three mandalas; Tirumular promises the body will last an aeon, 762 hopes for the light of a hundred crore moons.
